paragraphs: Chapter 1131
Episode 258. The Predator of All Dimensions (21)
Those who were fighting were all constantly looking up at the sky.

It was because of the raining, sharp light. The light, which could not be blocked by shields or weapons, was so fast that even superhumans found it difficult to read its trajectory. Moreover, for most of those fighting on the ground, dodging was almost impossible as they were floundering in the crimson seawater.
They could only stare wide-eyed and pray. That the light would miss them just one more time, so they could fight for the world even for a moment longer, even if it was a meaningless resistance.
In the midst of that, the fighters' gazes were captivated by a particularly brilliant streak of light. It was not a light fired by Kelliark.
Is that... a shooting star...?
In the midst of the rampant blood and death, a streak of light was falling to the ground, leaving a beautiful tail like a shooting star. It was in the direction of the battlefield.
For some reason, it felt like they should make a wish. The despair was so terrible and continuous that they wanted to cling to even such a superstition as shooting stars and wishes.
The moment the Coalition members looking up at the sky unconsciously had such a thought, the light that had neared the ground had taken the form of a person.
"Youngest!?"
"Brother Jin...!?"
Those defending the central front, and the Genesis Knights who had been protecting Jin and searching for the legacy, were all surprised. None of them knew that time had been stopped.
Chu-haaaak-!
A giant wave of light that shot out from Bradamante's blade cut through the red wave that was about to crash down on the Genesis Knights. Jin landed where the wave had collapsed and raised his head.
What happened? Chiron and Vahn did not ask. They simply read the fact that Jin's left arm and energy had been restored and nodded their heads.
Orgal and Enya were on Vahn's back. Orgal's consciousness was still fading in and out, and Enya was about to ask about Valeria but gritted her teeth.
"This way was correct, Father. The entrance to the sanctuary is about three thousand paces ahead, hidden by the red sea."
Jin offered Bradamante to Chiron. It meant he wanted to switch swords.
"You are not yet the patriarch, youngest. So be sure to bring it back."
"Of course."
The two men's swords were switched.
Barisada, now in Jin's grasp, vibrated heavily a couple of times. As if it had missed Temar, as if it was acknowledging Jin.
Soon, Jin dodged a light that fell towards the top of his head and offered Sigmund to Vahn as well.
"For some reason, I don't think it will be needed in the legacy, sister. Please provide cover. I will increase my speed alone."
There was no reason to move in a group anymore. Since he was the one Kelliark wanted to kill the most, it was a better move to move alone and draw his attacks to save his allies.
"Alright. I'll hold onto it, so you have to come back for it. Go!"
Trampling on Kelliark's desire, Jin leaped with all his might and began to move forward. Several streaks of light grazed his cheek and thigh threateningly.
"...Time? Surely the world didn't just stop for you?"
Kelliark's voice, the malice contained within it, stabbed at Jin's back. Even while blinded, he had instantly recognized that time had stopped. Otherwise, Jin could not be alive.
"How absurd. To think the leader of the Gray Owl had this much power."
She hid it well all this time, never once showing it even when the rebels were collapsing so badly. It makes sense that Silyn would lose her.
Kelliark swallowed his next words and shook his head. The complacent moments of the past were now tripping him up, just before he became the one true god.
He felt like he was being played.
Heluram had blinded him as if she knew this future would come, and the leader of the rebels had stopped time, albeit for a moment, without the Origin Stone or Kinzelo's authority.
Thanks to that, Jin, who should have died a hundred times over, was rising again like an immortal and heading towards Solderet's legacy.
"Then I'll destroy the whole world. Until nothing that moves and sacrifices for you is left."

A ringing sound, like jagged chunks of metal grinding in his head, arose. His neck and shoulders grew hot with the blood that flowed from his ears. Jin paid no mind and moved forward, dodging the light and creating cracks in the tidal waves.
"Protect the Young Patriarch!"
"Vamel Alliance, all who are alive, cover Brother Jin!"
Kuguguguk...! Swaaaak!
The battlefield trembled, and the red sea was growing more ferocious. The sun shining behind Kelliark's back had moved even closer to the ground and was causing explosions in all directions.
And that was not a phenomenon happening only on the battlefield.
The world.
Earthquakes and storms were spreading throughout the entire 33rd dimension. The crimson water now replaced all the rivers and seas of the world, and the sun was floating like a tumor in every sky.

Those who felt the vibrations anywhere in the world collapsed like diseased trees, and a wind sharper than a blade tore their bodies. The corpses were scorched by the sun, became black stains, and then disappeared.

"Can you feel this land, this world, your homeland dying? You can. Everyone can feel it. This is the price for loving Jin Runcandel. What are you trying to protect? Do you think you can dare to protect even a single grain of sand from this land from me?"

In the city of swords, Kalon, in the city of magic, Draca, in the Empire that had lost its capital, in the Secret Palace, in Tikan, and even in the small, harmless lands that had never been touched by the hand of all that power.
Disaster was spreading everywhere. Kelliark's hatred had annihilated seventy percent of all life in this world in less than a minute.
Ten minutes, no. It seemed that in just five more minutes, there would not be a single living, breathing creature left in the world.
Life cannot survive in a world with no ground to step on, no water to moisten, not even a sky to look at. Even if all life were as strong as Chiron, that would never change.
As Kelliark said, everyone was feeling that fact. It was as clear as a brand, even amidst the pain of their entire bodies burning, being torn, and being submerged.

No light of regeneration was left anywhere. The golden light that had illuminated the underworld, the golden souls that had remained in the Holy Kingdom, were being absorbed by the red sea and disappearing.
"Still, we just do what we can."

Jin said without stopping his run. The darkness left by Heluram was still blocking Kelliark's eyes and senses. Jin had been pierced by the light and had fallen into the sea, nearly losing his life several times, but each time, someone had helped him.
It wasn't just those who had reached the pinnacle of martial arts like Chiron and Vahn who were helping. One didn't have to be a superhuman to help Jin either.
Anyone who was next to Jin as he ran, anyone who could extend a hand, could do it.
They took the light for Jin, fell into the water for Jin. In other words, they died for him. They sacrificed.

Since the world was ending, sacrifice, paradoxically, no longer required such a great resolve. If no one could defy death anyway, then extending a hand for someone would be closer to preserving one's dignity than to sacrifice.
Especially if that someone was hope.
If it was the one and only possibility to punish the one who had brought the world to this state, then by all means.

"You're blind too, so you're just doing what you can to stop me, to stop us, aren't you, Kelliark Zipples? We must look ridiculous to you, right? The same goes for you. You're destroying the whole world, yet in the end, you can't kill a single person, me."
For a moment, Kelliark was at a loss for words.
He was destroying the entire world, yet he couldn't kill just one person. What was the reason? It wasn't because Jin was that strong. Even Chiron and Vahn couldn't go against the disaster.
Then was it because he hadn't become the one true god yet? Was that why he still lacked the power to change the unchangeable?
If the Origin Stone was fully restored and the Sun God's resurrection was perfectly complete, could he kill Jin Runcandel then?
Really, can I kill him? Even if I become the one true god, can I truly annihilate Jin Runcandel?
For the first time, a doubt arose.
If he acquired the full power of the whole Origin Stone and Kinzelo, there should be nothing impossible. According to the knowledge and experience Kelliark had accumulated, it should certainly be so.
But why couldn't he answer? If he said yes, why would it feel like a lie?

"That is what is truly ridiculous, Kelliark Zipfel. No matter how much you spout nonsense about being the one true god, no matter how many people we love you kill, no matter how you destroy the very land we must live on... You can't stop me from going in there."
That is your limit.
Jin continued his words and turned around.
He had run almost the entire three thousand paces. All that was left was about fifty paces, and the red sea covering the legacy.
In effect, all he had to do was part the sea.
But until now, Jin had dodged the waves that tried to crash down on him, and he had passed through the tidal waves by swinging his sword to create a gap within them.

Jin did not have the power to part the sea. He did not have the power to cut through this deep, red sea to the end and reach the legacy buried within it. It was something he could not do with the energy he had left.
Around that time, Kelliark had a gut feeling that Heluram's darkness would soon end.
'My senses will return soon. The legacy of Solderet is buried in the sea anyway, so as soon as my eyes open, I will kill Jin Runcandel in one blow...! I must do so!'

His heart was pounding like when he was human. He was so anxious he couldn't breathe. If by some chance Jin entered the legacy, he felt it would be painful. Even if he ended this world, that sense of powerlessness would never be forgotten.
But Jin hadn't just turned around. He hadn't turned around in frustration, thinking, is this the end?
Jin was certain.
'Someone will definitely come. Someone will come to open the sea... they must.'
He had turned around to see who it was.
And a moment later, Jin could see something black, like a waterspout, soaring up from beneath the red sea in the distance.
"It's you. Yes. I thought it would be you. I hoped it would be you."
Murakan.
The guardian dragon of Jin Runcandel, who had been sunk in the red sea, consumed by illusions. He was flying towards Jin.
[Kid!]
"Murakan, part this place!"

Like all the others, he did not ask why. Murakan immediately swung his two wings and spewed his breath. Because he knew that people had protected him, because he knew that they had somehow shielded him, he poured out his shadow energy more desperately than at any other time in the past three thousand years.
That breath bored a giant hole in the center of the red sea.
Within it, a barrier as dark as midnight was shimmering. It was the entrance to Solderet's final sanctuary.
